title: How to Spend Money Without Ruining Your Life — Morgan Housel
description:
In Episode 296 of the Moonshots Podcast, Mike and Mark kick off a brand new series on money with Morgan Housel’s The Art of Spending Money.

Money is on everybody’s mind.

The cost of living keeps rising. Many people are living paycheck to paycheck. Relationships are strained by financial pressure. And everywhere we look, we are encouraged to spend more, upgrade more, and chase the next bigger, faster, shinier thing.

But Morgan Housel invites us to ask a better question:

What is money actually for?

In this episode, Mike and Mark explore the psychology of spending, the trap of lifestyle inflation, and the quiet power of knowing what is enough. They unpack why so many people become captive to their spending, why status purchases rarely create lasting happiness, and why financial freedom often comes from spending less than you earn.

The conversation begins with the story of the Vanderbilts and the danger of building a life that owns you. Mike and Mark then explore practical ways to spend more wisely, including delaying purchases, avoiding spontaneous dopamine spending, buying second-hand, choosing experiences over status, and experimenting with what actually brings you joy.

They also reflect on the bigger idea behind Morgan Housel’s work: money should create peace, freedom, control, and contentment — not stress, debt, and comparison.

In this episode, you’ll learn:

• Why spending can quietly become a trap
• How lifestyle inflation steals your freedom
• Why bigger houses, faster cars, and fancier brands may not make you happier
• How to experiment with what you genuinely enjoy spending money on
• Why “I have enough” might be the most powerful money mantra
• How experiences can create more lasting satisfaction than things
• Why financial freedom starts with living within your means
• How to spend money in a way that supports your best life

This is a Moonshots episode for anyone who wants to rethink money, reduce financial stress, and make wiser choices with their time, energy, and resources.

Because the goal is not just to earn more.

The goal is to spend better.

Listen now and discover how to get out of the money trap, spend with intention, and find contentment in having enough.
